# teams agent create

Create an Agent 365 agent identity

## Usage

```
teams agent create [name] [options]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `name` | Agent name | No |

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--json` | [OPTIONAL] Output as JSON |
<!-- AUTOGENERATED:END -->

## Details

Creates an [Microsoft Agent 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/developer/registration) agent identity in a single command: it detects (and, with confirmation, installs) the [Agent 365 CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-cli) .NET global tool, verifies your Azure CLI and Teams login are on the same tenant, then runs `a365 setup all` to provision the agent blueprint, managed identity, and an **Agentic User** account.

> **Agentic User:** this command always creates an **Agentic User** (AI teammate account) alongside the agent blueprint — a plain identity-only blueprint can never be installed or used from Teams, Copilot, or Copilot Studio, so there's no flag to opt out. The messaging endpoint is always deferred at creation time (set it afterwards with `teams agent update-endpoint`, once your agent is deployed).

### Prerequisites

- Logged in: `teams login`
- [.NET 8+](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) installed (required to run the Agent 365 CLI)
- Signed in to the same tenant with the Azure CLI (`az login`) as with `teams login`
- Sufficient Entra permissions to create an agent blueprint (Global Administrator recommended; see [Admin Consent](#admin-consent) below if you're not one)

### Examples

Create interactively (prompts for an agent name if not provided):

```bash
teams agent create
```

Create a named agent identity:

```bash
teams agent create "My Support Agent"
```

Machine-readable output for CI/agent use:

```bash
teams agent create "My Support Agent" --json --yes
```

### Admin Consent

If you aren't a Global Administrator, `a365 setup all` may finish without granting the required OAuth2 permission consents. In that case `teams agent create` still exits successfully and reports `status: "pending_admin_consent"`, printing a consent URL (when available) that a Global Administrator can use to finish granting permissions. Re-run `teams agent create` after consent is granted to confirm `status: "completed"`.

### Output

On success (human mode), outputs the agent blueprint ID, managed identity principal ID, messaging endpoint (if already registered via `teams agent update-endpoint`), and the path to the generated `a365.generated.config.json`. With `--json`, outputs an object shaped like:

```json
{
  "status": "completed",
  "agentBlueprintId": "...",
  "agentBlueprintObjectId": "...",
  "managedIdentityPrincipalId": "...",
  "generatedConfigPath": "/path/to/a365.generated.config.json"
}
```

### Scope

This command always creates an Agentic User, so the resulting agent can actually be installed and used from Teams/Copilot. It does not yet cover custom Azure infrastructure options (SKU/region) or GCC/GCC-High/DoD clouds. See the [design doc](https://github.com/microsoft/teams-sdk/blob/main/packages/cli/docs/designs/agent-identity-design.md) for the full rationale and rollout plan.
